etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English stepchild, stepchyld, from Old English stēopċild (“stepchild”), equivalent to step- +‎ child. Compare Dutch stiefkind (“stepchild”), German Stiefkind (“stepchild”), Swedish styvbarn (“stepchild”).

definitions.definition: The child of one's spouse from a previous relationship.

quote.citation: 2024 August 3, Paula Span, “When Elder Care Is All in the Stepfamily”, in The New York Times‎[1]:
quote.text: Calculating the growth in stepfamilies isn’t simple, but a demographic analysis published last year estimated that about 16 percent of Americans over age 70 have at least one stepchild.  […]  Overall, stepchildren provide less care to older adults

definitions.definition: (obsolete) A bereaved child; one who has lost father or mother.
